title: Ensemble fragmentation debug log
content:
Goals / context:
- Investigate a recurring failure class when combining multiple exemplar fragments (I call it "ensemble fragmentation"). Observed when mixing short persona fragments + domain facts + task instructions. Outputs drift or hallucinate parts of different exemplars, or drop constraints entirely.
- Practical objective: find lightweight template transformations and selection heuristics that are robust under token budget constraints (<= 240 tokens prompt) and noisy paraphrases.
- Constraints: quick, reproducible experiments I can run in the playground / local harness; prefer techniques that can be translated into the prompt-library as a utility function (e.g., compactify_exemplars, anchor-instruction).

Quick hypothesis checklist:
1) Fragmentation is amplified when exemplars contain overlapping named entities (same characters, different attributes).
2) Token budget causes truncation of instruction anchors at the end of the prompt leading to implicit instruction-loss.
3) Model's attention allocation across exemplars is skewed when exemplar separation tokens are weak (just newlines) vs explicit markers (--- EXAMPLE N ---).
4) Paraphrase diversity in exemplars can act like a noisy ensemble causing the model to average inconsistent labels instead of selecting one.

Experiment matrix (what I need to run):
- Variables:
  - exemplar separator: [blank line, "---", "Example N:"]
  - anchor placement: [top-of-prompt instruction, post-exemplars summary anchor, prefix anchors per exemplar]
  - exemplar ordering: [random, clustered-by-persona, cluster-by-domain-fact]
  - exemplar compression: [unaltered, compressive-summaries, extractive-key-value pairs]
  - ensemble voting fallback: [single-call, n-call-vote(3), cached-embedding-sim-match]
  - temp: [0.0, 0.2, 0.6]
- Metrics to collect:
  - instruction-satisfaction rate (manual label 0/1 per output)
  - hallucination flag (manual quick triage: yes/no)
  - token usage (prompt+response)
  - cross-entropy on predicted label vs expected (when label data available)
  - embedding cosine drift between exemplar intents and final outputs

Protocol notes (how I run a trial):
1) Pick a seed task (FAQ rewrite, persona-consistent product explanation, roleplay customer reply). I most often use the "product explanation" microtask because it surfaces factual collisions.
2) Build 3 exemplars that intentionally overlap on name "Arin" but vary: one says Arin is an engineer, one says Arin leads product, one says Arin is a contractor. Controlled collision.
3) Run across separator types and anchor placements; temperature grid of [0.0, 0.2, 0.6].
4) Collect outputs, label quickly: did the model keep the anchor instruction? Did it conflate attributes? Did it invent new facts?

Representative prompt variants (small):
- BASE (compact exemplars, explicit anchors on top)
Instruction: You are to produce a concise product explanation for a non-technical audience. Keep it under 80 words. Do not invent details about the person's role.

--- Example 1 ---
Name: Arin
Role: Software engineer
Experience: built ML infra at two startups
Tone: approachable

--- Example 2 ---
Name: Arin
Role: Product lead
Experience: ran roadmap and customer interviews
Tone: concise

--- Example 3 ---
Name: Arin
Role: Contractor (integration)
Experience: short-term systems integrations
Tone: technical

Input: Write a 2-sentence blurb describing Arin's role for the team page.

- COMPRESSED (extractive key-value only)
Instruction: Same as above.
[EX1] Arin | role=software engineer | exp=ml infra
[EX2] Arin | role=product lead | exp=roadmap
[EX3] Arin | role=contractor | exp=integrations
Input: Write a 2-sentence blurb...

- PER-EXEMPLAR-ANCHOR (anchor after each example to bind):
Instruction: As above.
EX1: (Follow the instruction: product explanation, non-technical, no invented roles)
Name: Arin...
EX2: (Follow the instruction: product explanation, non-technical, no invented roles)

Failure cases observed so far (notes):
- Base, blank-line separator, anchor at top, temp=0.6: model produced a 3-sentence blurb that said "Arin is a product engineer who leads roadmap and also does integrations" — merged all roles. Hallucination: moderate.
- Compressed, temp=0.0: model produced a minimal blurb focusing on "software engineer" which is ok but dropped customer-facing detail; instruction satisfied.
- Per-exemplar-anchor, explicit --- separators, temp=0.2: best instruction satisfaction rate so far but sometimes overly literal (repeats phrases from exemplars).
- When exemplars use divergent tones (approachable vs technical) the model oscillates; explicit tone anchor reduces oscillation.

First-pass mitigations (ideas to test / implement in library):
1) Compact canonicalizers: transform exemplars into 2-line canonical KV rows (Name | role | primary_responsibility) to reduce noise and token count.
2) Anchor reinforcement: duplicate the instruction in a 1-line "binding anchor" after the exemplar block (e.g., "BIND: obey top instruction, do not combine roles"). Test whether repetition reduces mixing.
3) Separator token strength: prefer explicit labeled separators (e.g., "--- EXAMPLE 2 ---") instead of blank lines.
4) Exemplar clustering at insertion time: detect overlapping entity mentions across exemplars and either deduplicate (merge entries) or prefer exemplars that match the target domain.
5) Post-call ensemble: if initial output fails the anchor check, trigger 2 additional calls with temperature 0.0 and 0.2 and take the shortest output that matches anchor heuristics.

Short diagnostics I can add to harness:
- Anchor-checker: simple regex-based verifier that asserts prohibited phrases are absent and required constraints present (e.g., "role:" exact match).
- Entity-collision detector: pass exemplars through NER and flag overlapping entity spans. If >1 collision, try compressive summarization.
- Compression utility: greedy key-extraction that keeps at most 12 tokens per exemplar by selecting nouns + role phrase.

Mini failure log (actual snippets):
- Input prompt variant: BASE, temp 0.6
  Model output: "Arin is a product engineer who built ML infrastructure and often is contracted for integrations."
  Notes: fused roles; invented connection between contractor timeline and infra work.

- Input prompt variant: COMPRESSED, temp 0.0
  Model output: "Arin is a software engineer who built ML infrastructure and helps the product team."
  Notes: safe, conservative, slightly added "helps the product team" — minor inference but acceptable.

Open questions / experiments to prioritize:
- Does duplicating a short binding anchor after each exemplar materially reduce attribute fusion? (quick A/B with 200 trials)
- For small token budgets (<180 prompt tokens), is compression + temp=0.0 strictly better than per-exemplar anchors at temp 0.2?
- Can we build a tiny heuristic that auto-merges exemplars with the same named entity before sending (merge conflicting attributes into a single disambiguation block)?

Next steps (this week):
- Implement exemplar canonicalizer in prompt-library utils (extractive_kv_compress) — target: convert arbitrary example text into 2 KV lines < 16 tokens each. Owner: me. ETA: 3 days.
- Run 3x50 short trials for all separator types with and without per-exemplar anchor; collect rudimentary metrics (satisfaction, hallucination). Owner: Ethan. ETA: 5 days.
- Prototype anchor-checker for harness to auto-trigger fallback voting. Owner: Sofia. ETA: 1 week.

Notes to self / rough heuristics (personal):
- When in doubt, prefer compression + deterministic temp because it reduces creativity that causes mixing.
- Anchors are cheap and often effective, but they add tokens; try the "micro-anchor": one short imperative token sequence (e.g., "BIND: no role merge.") placed after exemplars.
- If exemplar set has >2 collisions on entity X, switch to a single merged exemplar for X rather than three small ones.

Reference runs (IDs I used locally):
- run_2025-02-20_ensembleA (base / blank sep)
- run_2025-02-21_anchorB (explicit sep + per-exemplar anchors)

Scratch ideas for the prompt-library API:
- compactify_exemplars(ex_list, max_tokens=12) -> returns compressed_kv_rows
- bind_anchor(text, anchor_phrase, repeat_after_each=False) -> returns prompt_string
- exemplar_collision_merge(ex_list, key_fields=["Name"]) -> returns merged_exemplar_list

End log.
(contains informal notes, rough experimental log entries and next-action items — keep in users area)
